newsitem.title: USA: Activists arrested for disrupting grain loadings.
newsitem.headline: Activists arrested for disrupting grain loadings.

text.p: Seventeen protestors from the environmental group Greenpeace were arrested Thursday for disrupting grain loadings at Archer Daniels Midland Co.'s grain terminal here, authorities said.
Nine protestors chained themselves to the facility's front gate, while eight others chained themselves inside two soybean barges, police and Greenpeace representatives said.

Authorities were still working in the afternoon to cut loose four of the protestors inside the barges, Greenpeace spokesman Paul Clarke said. The other 13 had been cut free and booked. He said all 17 were charged with criminal trespass.
Greenpeace said in a statement that its activists had "occupied" the Destrehan facility and halted loadings to protest exports of genetically-altered soybeans.
"Today's action marks Day Four of the week-long Greenpeace protest against the release of genetically-engineered soybeans into the marketplace," the statement said.
The altered soybeans are designed to tolerate Monsanto Co's "Roundup Ready" herbicide.
"At the very least they should be separated and labeled as genetically-engineered so consumers can choose whether they want to buy them," Greenpeace spokeswoman Terri Johnson said.
Thursday morning, an ADM employee at the terminal who declined to be named said, "They (protestors) are all over the place out here."
"We are not loading right now. We have the police department out here," the ADM employee said before hanging up.
An ADM spokesman at the company's headquarters in Decatur, Ill., was not available for comment.
The Destrehan terminal has storage capacity of more than six million bushels and a loading rate of 50,000 bushels per hour, according to industry sources.
